# Thanksgiving Hymns Column 18 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 1QHa (Cave 1), Col. 18 | **Condition:** heavily damaged

---

**18:1** [...] for the wicked [...] snares of wickedness [...]

**18:2** [...] and in their council of deceit they have plotted against me [...]

**18:3** [...] they have closed every source of understanding and concealed the drink of knowledge.

**18:4** And for their thirst [...] they look upon their folly [...]

**18:5** [...] at their feasts [...] for they have set [...]

**18:6** [...] and they have banished me from my land like a bird from its nest,

**18:7** and all my companions and friends have been driven from me.

**18:8** They regard me as a broken vessel; and they, interpreters of lies and seers of deceit,

**18:9** they have devised against me a scheme of Belial, to exchange Your instruction,

**18:10** which You have engraved upon my heart, for smooth things to Your people.

**18:11** They have withheld the drink of knowledge from the thirsty, and for their thirst

**18:12** they give them vinegar to drink. [...] their wickedness [...]

**18:13** [...] and gates of affliction without escape [...] and instruments of war [...]

**18:14** [...] and the bar upon my bones [...] like a ship in the fury of [...]

**18:15** [...] and they roar like the waves of the sea. [...] counselors of deceit [...]

**18:16** [...] and the scheme [...] like an encirclement upon me.

**18:17** My soul within me is faint [...] for my strength has departed from my flesh,

**18:18** and my heart is poured out like water, and my flesh melts like wax,

**18:19** and the strength of my loins has turned to fear, and my arm is torn from its socket.

**18:20** I cannot [...] for the hostility is [...] without remedy, and rebuke burns [...]

**18:21** [...] I cannot [...] my pain [...] and a sickness unto death [...]

**18:22** [...] but they [...] they rejoice [...] and upon me [...]

**18:23** [...] my arm [...] my foot sinks in the mire.

**18:24** [...] the snares of wickedness have enclosed me [...] and nets [...]

**18:25** But You, O God, [...] You have set my soul in the bundle of the living,

**18:26** and You have protected me against all the snares of the pit. And men of violence

**18:27** have sought my soul, but they have not prevailed when You strengthened my heart

**18:28** and came to my aid. For by Your covenant-faithfulness [...] and by the abundance of Your mercies

**18:29** You have strengthened my standing, and in the greatness of Your forgiveness [...] You have not rejected me,

**18:30** and in the time of the anguish of my soul You have not abandoned me.

**18:31** [...] my cry [...] and to my groaning You have given an answer of consolation,

**18:32** and I have rejoiced in forgiveness, and I am comforted over the former transgression.

**18:33** I know that there is hope in Your covenant-faithfulness and trust in the abundance of Your might,

**18:34** for no one is justified without Your good pleasure, and no one [...] apart from Your will.

**18:35** [...] You teach all knowledge, and everything that exists is by Your will.

**18:36** And there is no other beside You to reply to Your counsel and to understand

**18:37** all Your holy purpose and to gaze into the depths of Your mysteries and to comprehend all Your wonders.

---
*EMET notes: Column 18 is heavily damaged but preserves powerful lament material. "Bundle of the living" (tzeror ha-chayyim) in line 25 alludes to 1 Samuel 25:29. Lines 28-37 shift to trust and consolation.*
